statement.p: Find the area of the region enclosed by the parametric equation

static.solution:
t = \sqrt {6} and t = -\sqrt {6} yields the same x and y coordinates, namely (0,54). These two values of t are going to be the upper and lower limits of integration.
The area under a curve defined by parameters x = f(t) and y = g(t) can be expressed A = \int ydx =\int g(t)f'(t)dt Plugging in the functions and the upper and lower limits of integration, we have A = \int_{-\sqrt{6}}^{\sqrt{6}} 9 t^2 (3 t^2 - 6) dt = (2) (9) \int_{0}^{\sqrt{6}} (3 t^4 - 6 t^2) dt = 18 \left[ \frac {3}{5} t^5 - \frac {6}{3} t^3 \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{6}} = 18 \left[ \frac {3}{5} 6^{5/2} - \frac {6}{3} 6^{3/2} \right] = 423.271827552933
